# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The light never holds. It changes every round, and it always walks the
same circle of five colours. What matters is what it shows at the
moment of the cut.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| yellow | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives a single condition: cut the green wire only when the light is yellow. Deaf must relay that to Blind, who can operate the bomb. Since I cannot speak, I will encode the phrase “CUT IF YELLOW GREEN” using the first 26 gesture symbols as A–Z and 🤳 as a word separator.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👌","✊","🤜","🤳","👆","🤟","🤳","🖖","✌","👉","👉","🫳","👋","🤳","🖐","🫸","✌","✌","🫲"])
```

|---|---|

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can cut wire positions 1, 2, or 3, but have no other tactile information. Please use the manual's gesture instructions to communicate with Deaf, and have Deaf relay the exact cut instruction to me by voice.
Deaf says to Mute: Bomb view: DISPLAY 0. LIGHT yellow. WIRES: 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

The current display is yellow and the green wire is position 3. Deaf needs a clear, compact visible indication of position three so they can relay the instruction to Blind. I will use three raised index-finger gestures to indicate wire 3.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👆", "👆", "👆"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display 0; light yellow; wires: position 1 blue, position 2 red, position 3 green. Please tell Deaf by gesture which position I must cut, and have Deaf relay it to me by voice.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: light is blue. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

The light has changed to blue, so cutting now would violate the manual. I will signal “do not cut / wait” to Deaf. When Deaf next reports yellow, I will signal position 3 again.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✋"])
```

Blind says to Mute: Do not rely on the prior instruction yet: Deaf now reports the light is blue, not yellow. Current visible state remains display 0; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Please recalculate from the manual and gesture the current cut position to Deaf for verbal relay.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: light is now white. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

The manual still authorizes a cut only while the light is yellow. The reported current light is white, so there is no cut position to relay now. I will repeat an unambiguous stop/wait gesture to Deaf; when Deaf next sees yellow, the required position remains 3.

```text

```

Blind says to Mute: Deaf now reports: display 0, light white, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. I cannot safely interpret one open-hand gesture as a wire position. For the current state, please signal the cut position unambiguously to Deaf: one raised index for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, three fingers for wire 3; or signal no cut/wait with an open hand.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: light is now red. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

The light is red, not yellow. The manual therefore says no cut now. Blind has specified that an open hand means wait/no cut, so I will send that exact signal to Deaf for verbal relay.

Please, when the manual says to cut, gesture exactly: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or three raised fingers for wire 3. Use 🖐 only to mean wait/no cut. Deaf will say the gesture aloud to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: light is now purple. Display remains 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

Deaf says to Mute: Update: light returned to yellow. Display 0; wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.

The light is yellow, and the manual requires cutting the green wire. Green is at position 3, so I will send the agreed single gesture for cut position 3.


On a later turn, send exactly the applicable one-symbol instruction based on the current bomb state. Do not send a cut symbol unless it is final.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: light is blue again. Display 0; wires remain 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green.
